V. ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS MINION CANNOT BE AVOIDED Wildlife
The Study area bounded by South 20th Street, W. Lavton Avenue, South howell Avenue, and W. College Avenue comprises 1,918 acres with land usage as listed in figure 13. This summary indicates the area is significantly changing due to urbanization. Approximately 40% of this area with its undeveloped lands, and marginal agricultural use lands could be considered as a limited urban wildlife habitat. The proposed 300° to 350° wide Airport Spur proposal represents only 6° of this habitat area.
On-site investigations indicate that game habitat and ground cover is generally lacking in this area. Unavoidable losses of existing vegetation will occur with the implementation of the project. The displacement of animal species in the construction area will also cause a temporary species conflict for cover and resting areas. Loss of grassy areas which provided minimal habitat will be largely replaced by landscaping the areas outside of the traveled roadways. This development will result in additional habitation and the landscaping, plantings and grasses involved may prove to be attractive to some forms of wildlife. Wildlife displacement is continually taking place as the study area experiences urbanization and extensive land use.
Land Acquisition and Relocation
The proposed freeway project will incorporate approximately 35 acres of land which will be removed from the local tax base. This acquisition amounts to about $2.5 million. However, capital investments and productivity of commercial and industrial interests developing adjacent to the project have already offset this temporary loss.
